bounds: One platform queue and one session key. Two enqueues after removal, four unique lease identities, and time 0..6. TTL 3 and lease 1 preserve the relevant expiry ordering. The action projection assumes serialized coordinator calls and a durable entry write or deletion. A lost response and coordinator restart retain committed writes. Batch scanning, Redis compatibility, external provider delivery and session transcript authority are separate.

assumptions: No scheduling fairness. Only the exact current lease can remove the stored entry.
No scheduling fairness. Lease identities are unique and the coordinator serializes requests.
No scheduling fairness. A committed entry and lease survive a lost reply or restart.
Weak fairness of dropStale. A stale entry eventually appears in a drain scan and its deletion succeeds. Acknowledgement may retire the entry first.
No scheduling fairness. A stale entry can persist without a successful drain or acknowledgement.
